question: Find the circumference (in m) of the largest circle that can be drawn completely inside a rectangle whose dimensions are given as 249 m and 168 m. (Take π = (22)/(7))
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The largest circle inscribed completely inside a rectangle has its diameter equal to the shorter side (breadth) of the rectangle.

Diameter of circle (d) = Breadth of rectangle = 168 m

Circumference = π × d = 22/7 × 168

⇒ Circumference = 22 × 24 = 528 m

**∴ The correct answer is 528 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the rectangle (l) = 249 m

Breadth of the rectangle (b) = 168 m

 
 
 
• 
 d = 168 m
 Length = 249 m
 168 m

**Formula Used:**

Circumference of a circle = 2 × π × r

**Calculations:**

⇒ To fit completely inside the rectangle without crossing the boundaries, the circle's diameter cannot exceed the rectangle's smallest dimension.

⇒ Maximum possible diameter (d) = Breadth = 168 m

⇒ Radius (r) = 168 ÷ 2 = 84 m

⇒ Circumference = 2 × (22/7) × 84

⇒ Circumference = 2 × 22 × 12

⇒ Circumference = 44 × 12 = 528 m

**∴ The correct answer is 528 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Largest Circle in a Rectangle

The maximum diameter is always bounded by the shorter side of the rectangle. Diameter = breadth.

Largest Square in a Circle

When a square is perfectly inscribed inside a circle, the diagonal of the square is equal to the diameter of the circle. Side of square = d ÷ √2.

Circumcircle of a Rectangle

For a circle circumscribing a rectangle (touching all four corners), the diagonal of the rectangle serves as the diameter of the circle. Diameter = √(l² + b²).
